title: refactor(tooling): shard the ADR-anchor registry one file per anchor
body:
Part of #6957 — this is the `scripts/adr-anchors.json` half only. `packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts` belongs to the `domain:spec` seat and is the file their in-flight retirement cards are appending to right now; restructuring it from this lane mid-window would cause the exact collision the card documents. It is being transferred to that seat separately, so `Part of` rather than `Fixes`.

## Ruling this implements

Maintainer ruling of 2026-08-10, quoted verbatim and untranslated:

> **hybrid — batch now, split the append surface as the durable fix.**
> Now: the PM landing relay batches same-window retirement cards into one PR … Queued: implement per-card registry entry files concatenated by a generator, the `.changeset/*.md` shape that already de-conflicted this repo's other hottest file; `scripts/adr-anchors.json` is in the same fix space and may ride the same mechanism. Option B (uncommitted build-time artifacts) is rejected — the review diff of `spec-changes.json` / the upgrade guide is worth the laps it costs.

Option (a) adopted, (b) rejected, (c) is the interim mitigation. None re-opened here.

## What changed

`scripts/adr-anchors.json` — a single 343-line append-only array that every card adding an anchor had to edit — becomes **`scripts/adr-anchors/`, one JSON file per anchor**, 47 of them, named for the path each anchors (`packages/objectql/src/engine.ts` → `packages__objectql__src__engine.ts.json`). A new module `scripts/adr-anchors.mjs` assembles them in id order at read time; `scripts/check-adr-anchors.mjs` consumes that instead of parsing one file.

Also updated: the three live pointers at the old path (`AGENTS.md` PD #13, the `lint.yml` step comment, two runtime code comments). Records under `docs/adr/`, historical changesets and `content/docs/releases/` are deliberately untouched — and the path prefix `scripts/adr-anchors` still resolves for a reader who greps it.

## Consumer verdict is unchanged

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `check:adr-anchors` verdict | OK | OK |
| anchored files checked | 47 | 47 |
| decision numbers audited | 118 | 118 |
| ambiguous-number note | 4 | 4 (same four, now id-ordered) |
| `--self-test` assertions | 39 | 52 |

The only figures that move are the citation-scan denominators (20837 → 20853 across 3418 → 3469 files): the same anchor text now lives in 47 tracked files instead of 1, which is inherent to the split and not a verdict change. Every failure message is byte-for-byte the same except that each now names the exact entry file to edit instead of the shared blob.

## The de-conflicting claim, demonstrated rather than asserted

Two simulated concurrent appends, replayed under both layouts with `git merge-tree --merge-base` — old base `origin/main`, new base this branch:

```
== OLD layout: two cards each append a DIFFERENT anchor ==
  adr-anchors.json (single file) -> CONFLICT (rc=1)
       CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in scripts/adr-anchors.json
== NEW layout: the SAME two appends ==
  adr-anchors/ (one file per anchor) -> CLEAN
== NEW layout CONTROL: two cards edit the SAME anchor (must NOT merge clean) ==
  same shard, two different edits -> CONFLICT (rc=1)
       CONFLICT (add/add): Merge conflict in scripts/adr-anchors/packages__proof__alpha.ts.json
```

The control is the half that is easy to skip and cannot be: a layout in which two edits to *one* entry also merge clean is a layout that silently loses one of them. Harness proven non-blind before any of this was believed — split-then-reassemble is byte-identical over all 47 entries, and flipping a single character in one invariant breaks that equality.

Reverse verification of the gate itself: deleting `ADR-0091` from `packages/core/src/security/grant-validity.ts` turns `check:adr-anchors` red with the invariant text and the shard path; restoring it returns green.

## Why a sharded directory and not a committed concatenated artifact

Because the card's subject is the **merge queue**, and this repo has already measured what that rules out. `merge=os-regen` (#4675) is a *local* git facility; the GitHub merge queue rebuilds each PR server-side where no custom merge driver runs, which is why #5837 had to **shard** the three hottest spec artifacts one file per category rather than merely route them. A checked-in aggregate here would be exactly that server-side conflict surface, and it would carry no review information the entry files do not already carry.

⚠️ To be explicit, since it is adjacent to the rejected option (b): **nothing left version control and no reviewable diff was traded away.** Every byte of the old file is still committed, one entry per file. The review diff improves — a new anchor is a new file rather than a hunk in a shared blob — and `spec-changes.json` / the upgrade guide are not touched by this PR at all.

## Two properties enforced, not assumed

- **The shard filename is a pure function of the entry id.** Different anchors ⇒ different files ⇒ clean merge; the same anchor ⇒ the same file ⇒ git conflict, as it must. `assembleAnchors` rejects a shard whose name disagrees with its `file`, so a rename cannot quietly re-open the losing half.
- **Order is derived (sort by id), never declared.** No index file: an index would itself be the single append-only file every card must edit, reintroducing the conflict being removed (PM decision on #6957). Order is not contractual for this registry in any case — the gate iterates to accumulate errors and never compares positions.

## Verification

```
$ node scripts/check-adr-anchors.mjs --self-test
✓ check-adr-anchors --self-test: 52 assertions over the real auditAdrDirectory() / auditCitedNumbers() / assembleAnchors() paths.
$ node scripts/check-adr-anchors.mjs
check-adr-anchors: OK (47 anchored file(s), every governing ADR still referenced; 118 decision number(s), each naming one decision or an allowlisted pair; 20853 citation(s) across 3469 file(s) resolve).
$ node scripts/check-adr-links.mjs
✅ check-adr-links: 531 relative link destination(s) under docs/adr/ resolve (8 frozen on the shrink-only baseline)
$ node scripts/check-nul-bytes.mjs
check-nul-bytes: OK (scanned 6701 text file(s) — 6701 tracked, 0 untracked-not-ignored; skipped 5 binary; no raw ASCII control bytes)
```

All four re-run after merging `origin/main` (no commit on main since the fork point touched the old registry, so nothing was dropped). No `check:`/`gen:` script entry was added or renamed, so the #4203 meta-gate surface is untouched; `.gitattributes` and `regen-artifacts.mjs` are likewise unchanged — this registry is hand-authored, not generator-owned.
